transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-27 14:00 UTC | Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rae (Redwood CSM) | Sara (Juniper), Diego (Juniper CTO), Priya (Infra), Mark (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — happy to see the team. quick check-in on capacity and the region add on.
[00:10] Sara: Hey, thanks. yep we have a traffic uptick, about 2x token throughput month over month for our payments fraud model. want to understand lead times for us-west and ap-southeast.
[00:22] Maya: Right. TL;DR we can provision dedicated pools for both regions; lead time depends on reserved capacity vs hosted burst — Liam maybe you want to give the perf/backing?
[00:30] Liam: Sure. so options: hosted API expansion is fastest (days), Dedicated reserved capacity for guaranteed SLOs is more like 2-3 weeks to schedule GPUs and network. for ap-southeast there's sometimes lead time for GPU availability but we can do a hybrid (hosted + dedicated fallback) while reserved is coming up.
[00:47] Diego: What about latency targets? our SLAs need p95 sub-200ms for single-turn reranking calls. is that realistic from ap-southeast?
[01:00] Liam: p95 < 200ms is challenging across long-haul; for small models and local edge routing it's doable. we usually recommend model sharding: keep the heavy decoder in dedicated in-region or use quantized variant for apac to hit latency. plus caching of prefixes (KV cash in the transcript) will help.
[01:20] Priya: can you clarify the "quantized variant" tradeoffs? we care about inference accuracy for fraud decisions.
[01:28] Liam: yeah, quantization (int8 / int4) reduces perf costs and often maintains accuracy within noise, but we should run evals on your prompt set. Redwood Optimize can recommend a profile; we'll add that to the benchmark.
[01:40] Sara: On security — we need SOC2 type II evidence and KMS integration. also need SSO with our IdP (SAML).
[01:49] Maya: absolutely, we'll share our SOC2 report and the KMS integration guide. On SSO, we support SAML and SCIM for provisioning. Rae, want to comment on timeline?
[01:58] Rae: For SSO we typically get a test SAML assertion in staging and can move to prod after validation. timeline 1-2 weeks depending on your IdP team.
[02:08] Mark: From procurement: contract extension vs new PO? we prefer an amendment to avoid reinstating security reviews. any blockers?
[02:16] Maya: amendment is fine. we'll draft a pricing addendum that shows the new committed throughput and the region pricing. Mark, you'll review that with your legal/procurement.
[02:25] Diego: curious about failover — if in-region capacity saturated, what happens? do requests route to another region and is that compliant with data residency?
[02:34] Liam: we have routing policies — you can set "no cross-border fallback" to enforce residency. alternatively, you can allow cross-region fallback for availability; we'll need to map which routes are residency-restricted. that's why we asked about APAC residency specifics.
[02:52] Priya: for APAC, data-at-rest must be in-country where possible (Singapore preferred), and keys in our KMS. can Redwood support external KMS / bring-your-own-key?
[03:03] Maya: yes, BYOK via cloud KMS and HSM integrations are supported. we'll share the KMS runbook.
[03:11] Sara: perfect. next, pricing. we currently spend roughly $60k/mo and want a committed uplift to cover expected growth — what sort of discounts on reserved capacity?
[03:22] Maya: for committed reserved capacity we tier discounts by commit size and term. for a 12-month uplift at 2x throughput we can propose a blended rate — I'll include a couple of tiers in the addendum.
[03:33] Mark: do those tiers include dedicated support SLAs? we need a 99.9% uptime SLA for core payment paths.
[03:41] Maya: yes, dedicated + enterprise support gives you the SLA package; we'll put the SLA terms in the amendment.
[03:48] Diego: technical deep dive: Liam, can you walk through the benchmark plan and what logs you'll need?
[03:54] Liam: sure. we'll run a 2-hour throughput run in your staging with a production-like prompt mix. we'll capture token-level latency, GPU utilization, queue depths, and KV cache hit rates. ideally provide a sample of your prompt set and a staging API key.
[04:12] Sara: we can provide a limited prompt set and staging key. Priya will coordinate.
[04:18] Priya: yes I'll set up a staging key and share network peering details — question though: will Redwood need inbound rules to our VPC or do you use outbound-only?
[04:28] Liam: for Private deployments we usually set up VPC peering or private link. for hosted/dedicated we can do outbound only for calls but for private deployment we need network connectivity. we'll document both options in the SOW.
[04:41] Speaker 1: [laughter] okay.
[04:44] Maya: timeline wise — proposed milestones: pricing addendum and SOW by 2 days, staging benchmark run next week, SOC2 + ksm docs shared today, procurement to sign amendment by early Feb. does that align?
[04:59] Mark: that's fine but need one more: can we get a short run-book showing rollback/fallback ops for incidents? compliance needs that.
[05:07] Rae: yes we'll include an incident response summary and runbook excerpt.
[05:12] Diego: about canary / rollout — we want canary traffic at 10% for 48 hours before full cutover. supported?
[05:20] Liam: yes, Redwood rollouts support canary A/B and automatic fallback policies if we detect error/regressions. we'll also instrument quality monitoring so you can flag regressions on prompt sets.
[05:33] Sara: any gotchas with multi-model routing? we sometimes route different models for fraud scoring and explanation paths.
[05:40] Liam: the runtime supports per-route model pinning. you can route one path to a smaller quantized model and another to a full-precision model and do cross-route tracing. there's some overhead for cross-model KV cache reuse, but we can measure in the benchmark.
[05:57] Priya: I heard "KV cash" from earlier — is that like a persisted cache?
[06:03] Liam: yeah, KV cache, it stores recent key-value attention states to avoid recomputing prefixes. it helps reduce latency for chat-like flows or repeated prefixes.
[06:12] Diego: any compliance review needed for APAC?
[06:16] Maya: sometimes local data residency needs an attestation; we'll work with legal to fill any forms.
[06:21] Sara: for the staging benchmark, what sample RPS should we target? current peak is ~600 rps token-requests during mid-day; we expect 1200 rps in two months.
[06:31] Liam: let's target 1.5x of your projected peak in staging (so start at ~1800 rps simulated), that will surface autoscaling behavior.
[06:38] Maya: quick operational Q: will logs show token-level costs per route?
[06:43] Rae: yes, Console provides token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency and spend. we can provision access for your finance or infra team.
[06:50] Mark: procurement asks for a contract term option: 12 vs 24 months with pricing breaks. can you show both?
[06:56] Maya: yes, I'll include both in the addendum.
[07:01] Priya: network — do you support peering in ap-southeast?
[07:05] Liam: yes, though vendor availability can vary; if peering not available we use private link or dedicated interconnect through a partner.
[07:13] Diego: what's the expected cutover downtime for migrating traffic?
[07:17] Liam: negligible if you do a gradual canary and warm KV caches; the bigger risk is cold-start latency spikes for large models without warmed caches. that's why we suggest warmup runs in the staging benchmark.
[07:31] Sara: will Redwood run the warmup or do we run it from our side?
[07:35] Liam: we can help run warmup scripts as part of the benchmark or provide them for you to execute. we'll coordinate.
[07:43] Speaker 2: [brief crosstalk] yeah that sounds good.
[07:47] Maya: any blockers to moving forward?
[07:49] Sara: KMS integration timeline — need to confirm with security team.
[07:53] Priya: confirm we need BYOK and prefer keys in our cloud KMS, not Redwood managed keys.
[07:59] Maya: noted — we'll mark that as required.
[08:02] Mark: procurement will need a sample amendment doc to review with legal.
[08:07] Maya: I'll attach a draft.
[08:09] Diego: small ask — can we get bench results with annotated breakdowns for latency contributors? sockets, queueing, gpu stalls?
[08:18] Liam: yes, we'll include a perf breakdown and a short dashboard snapshot.
[08:22] Rae: also we'll include quality regression checks against your golden prompt set.
[08:26] Sara: timeline recap?
[08:29] Maya: pricing addendum + SOW by 2027-01-29, staging key/setup by Priya asap, benchmark run by Liam and results by 2027-02-02, procurement review and sign week of 2027-02-07.
[08:43] Diego: sounds good.
[08:45] Maya: any other questions?
[08:46] Priya: small note — we may need additional IP & audit language in the amendment; Mark will raise that.
[08:52] Mark: yep will flag.
[08:55] Speaker 3: thanks everyone.
[08:57] Maya: thanks team — we'll follow up in email with artifacts.
